subject: Provisioning slab model for private GPU farms
messages:
From: Raj Patel <raj@acmerobotics.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@acmerobotics.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Private pool sizing — target throughput & headroom

Jonas —

Thanks for taking this on. We're trying to lock down a proposal for a VPC/private deployment of ~40 GPUs across two racks. Our product team wants an ops-run private pool that can hit the following:
- Sustained directional throughput of ~9k tokens/sec for our multimodal endpoint during peak windows (model: mix of mPT-7B variants + quantized 13B family)
- Spiky bursts up to ~18k tokens/sec for 3–5 minute windows, ~2–3x/day

Questions we need answered for the procurement/OPS teams:
1) Can you propose a provisioning model that makes burst capacity predictable without paying for full-time idle GPUs?
2) What's the recommended warm/cold cache strategy and how much headroom should we reserve for safe fallbacks?
3) Network egress / cross-rack headroom constraints — do you expect NLB-level bottlenecks at the numbers above?

Attached is our current infra diagram and a csv of historical QPS by endpoint. Happy to jump on a quick call to walk it through.

Thanks,
Raj
Ops lead — Acme Robotics
[Attachment: acme-infra-topology.pdf (PDF, 320KB)]

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Raj Patel <raj@acmerobotics.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private pool sizing — target throughput & headroom

Raj —

Thanks for the diagram and the numbers. I sketched a pragmatic "slab" provisioning model below that we use internally for private farms when customers want predictable bursts without continuous overprovisioning. TL;DR: carve the pool into immutable slabs you can attach/detach for bursts + a small warm slab kept live for steady-state.

Proposal (high level):
- Slabs: define three slab sizes mapped to GPU counts and expected sustained throughput:
  - Small slab = 4x A100-80GB (Sustained: ~1.8–2.4k tokens/sec; Burst cap: ~4.5k)
  - Medium slab = 8x A100-80GB (Sustained: ~3.6–4.8k tokens/sec; Burst cap: ~9k)
  - Large slab = 16x A100-80GB (Sustained: ~7.2–9.6k tokens/sec; Burst cap: ~18k)
- For your 40 GPUs we recommend: baseline = 1 Medium slab (8 GPUs) kept warm + 3 Small slabs staged cold (24 GPUs) + 8 GPUs reserved for control/ops/eviction handling. That maps to baseline sustained ~4k tokens/sec with on-demand burst to ~13–14k by attaching two small slabs fast. Full large-burst (~18k) requires activating the large slab (recomposition of small->large).

Key operational controls:
- Warm vs cold: keep baseline slab(s) warm (hot kernels, KV cache warmed for common prefixes). Cold slabs are pre-initialized images with model weights on SSD; warm-up time measured ~45–120s depending on model quantization.
- Cache policy: prefix-based K/V caching with LRU eviction; reserve 20% of GPU VRAM across warm slabs for shared prefix hotset. Evict policy for cross-slab routing: prefer local KV hits, fallback to remote fetch with a soft-degraded latency SLA.
- Autoscale curve: attach slabs at 70% sustained utilization for baseline GPUs; detach when utilization < 30% for 5 minutes. For bursts, allow manual or policy-driven attach at short notice; target attach latency <= 90s.
- Networking: plan for 25–30 Gbps per 8-GPU slab for peak mixtures (tensor / model IO + shard rebalancing). Cross-rack NLBs should be provisioned with 10% headroom above expected peak. For your topology (2 racks), we recommend redundant 100Gb links and an egress carve-out on the firewall for model fetch traffic to avoid burst throttling.

Attached: a quick slab-sizing spreadsheet and an example autoscale policy. I'm keeping the numbers conservative to preserve SLOs; we can tune once we run a short load test.

Next steps:
1) Ops: confirm whether you can reserve SSD-backed cold nodes for the cold slabs (we need ~1.2TB per node for quantized 13B artifacts).
2) Security: confirm KMS/HSM access patterns for model keys during slab attach.
3) Engineering: agree on target attach/detach latency (we can push to ~60s in most datacenters with image prefetching).

I'll loop the rest of the infra team for the eviction and warmup ops questions.

— Jonas
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: slab-sizing-proposal.xlsx (XLSX, 220KB)]

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Raj Patel <raj@acmerobotics.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private pool sizing — target throughput & headroom

Quick notes from the ops/security lens —

- Eviction & cache coherence: recommend a tiered eviction policy, not pure LRU. Hotset should be pinned per-slab for 60s after a burst to avoid repeated cold misses. On-disk eviction should prefer largest models first (13B family), keep smaller models resident when feasible.
- Warm-up optimizations: prefetch KV segments during off-peak windows (02:00–05:00 local) and maintain a lightweight heartbeat to prevent eviction of frequently used shards. This reduces attach latency by ~20–30s in our experience.
- Networking specifics: if you have cross-rack rovers (for shard rebalancing) expect short-lived traffic storms. Add a QoS policy to deprioritize background rebalancing when application latency > 150ms.
- Safety factors: for procurement, ask for a 15–20% buffer on GPU warranty & spare parts and a 30% buffer on disk IOPS for model downloads.

I'll prep a short runbook for attach/detach that maps to the autoscale thresholds Jonas suggested. Marissa — can you validate that the pricing/commercials for the reserved 8 GPUs are acceptable to the customer?

— Kim

Appreciate the concrete slab breakdown and the operational guidance. This is exactly the level we needed to justify the two-rack design. A few confirmations from our side:
- We can reserve the requested SSD-backed cold nodes (confirmed with infra team).
- KMS access: security says KMS is available but wants to review the HSM flow during slab attach; we'll share an access window next week.
- Procurement: please send a one-page commercial summary showing baseline vs burst sizing (what we pay reserved vs on-attach) and an example SLA for attach latency. Marissa — can you take point on that?

Once we have the one-pager and the runbook from Kim, we'll schedule a short 60-minute kickoff to agree final attach thresholds and test plan.

Thanks — looking forward to the test run.
Raj
Ops lead — Acme Robotics
